name: Bloodlord
body:
When one thinks of blood magic, their responses will be variable, sometimes depending on what they know of their own culture’s perspective on the idea, other times their opinions are influenced by the immense diversity out there in the literary marketplace about the concept. Yet, in many written stories, blood magic typically revolves around a singular protagonist or antagonist, the main character who does incredible things, often miraculous, with the aid of their bloodline and natural talents that eventually marks them above their peers as they strive to become something greater than themselves with hard work and their innate gifts, to reach beyond fate and destiny. You see this happening a lot in cultivation, transmigration, or even sci-fi novels, where one’s bloodline determines their natural talents, but it is their perseverance that takes them to the top. Their pursuit to better themselves, to adapt to the insurmountable challenges before them…and yet, many of them are considered anti-heroes, dark heroes, or straight up villains.

To us, that is the goal of the bloodlord – a character who delves into blood magic that helps them discover the secrets of their otherwise dormant bloodline, to grow outside the normal limits of their race, and pursue the truths of the world. Your bloodlord can be any alignment, they can be tragic heroes, insidious villains, and anything in between. The bloodlord touches upon many paths of possibilities and talents, taking what they need to survive and prosper in their world, but they rarely become masters with a singular focus on one field. Versatility and flexibility in body, mind, and soul is the strongest tool in the bloodlord’s survival bag.

Follow the sanguine paths and cut your own path in the world… whether it be with your own blood….or the blood of others.

Role: Bloodlords are capable of becoming skilled in just about any role you can conceive of, barring those that require the divine as a necessity. Whether they are solitary or a member of an adventuring group, bloodlords are often viewed with suspicion, for the uninitiated fear the ease at which bloodlord can manipulate the blood of others. A bloodlord may never match the same level of excellence as other classes in their specific roles, but they have more stamina and versatility that few can match.

Alignment: Any

Hit Die: d8

Starting Wealth: 2d6 × 10 gp (average 70 gp.) In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Base Attack Bonus: Determined by the sanguine path chosen.

Class Skills

The class skills for the Bloodlord are Craft (Int), Heal (Wis), Knowledge (local, nature) (Int), Perception (Wis), and Profession (Wis).

In addition, the bloodlord gains additional class skills from the sanguine path they selected as their specialization.

Skill Points Per Level: 4 + Intelligence Modifier

Class Features

The following are the class features of the bloodlord.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency

A bloodlord’s weapon and armor proficiencies are determined by the sanguine path they selected as their specialization.

Blood Bank (Ex)

When drawing fresh blood from an appropriate target via sanguine recycler, the bloodlord compresses and deposits the blood, which contains the stolen life essence and genetic information of the target, within an isolated internal storage that cannot be accessed by anyone other than the bloodlord.

Bloodlords cannot access the blood bank of other bloodlords. This ensures that the compressed foreign blood poses no risk to the bloodlord (such as poisoned blood, diseases, viruses, cancerous cells, etc.) and cannot be affected by any effect from any source other than the bloodlord, unless specifically allowed by the effect’s description.

The stored blood can remain indefinitely within the blood bank, until it is used by the bloodlord via their bloodlord class abilities or discarded as a free action by the bloodlord. The discarding of blood from the blood bank is usually expressed by harmlessly ejecting the blood out in a physical manner or simply erasing it from within the blood bank.

Beginning with 1st level, the bloodlord can store a maximum of 2 sanguine points per bloodlord class level in their blood bank.

At 5th level and every 5 bloodlord class levels thereafter, the amount of sanguine points the bloodlord can store in their blood bank increases by an additional 1 sanguine point per bloodlord class level, to a maximum of 6 sanguine points per bloodlord class level at 20th level (for a grand total of 120 sanguine points).

Blood Burn (Ex)

At 1st level, the bloodlord can “burn” their blood to fuel many of their class abilities and enhance such abilities described with the augmentation of each ability.

In a way, a bloodlord “burning” their blood via this class feature is similar to bleed damage in some aspects.

However, while blood burn is similar to bleed damage, neither bleed damage nor any other similar loss of hit points count as blood burn, including for its own augmentation.

The bloodlord can activate this ability to “burn” their blood as a move action, losing 1 hit point immediately, and 1 hit point at the beginning of each of their turns as long as the ability remains active. This loss of hit points can only be recovered through natural healing, including natural healing that was enhanced or altered by other abilities or effects, or through curative effects that restores hit points with the exception of continuous fast healing or regeneration.

Unlike bleed damage, the loss of hit points by blood burn can only be stopped by the bloodlord going unconscious, dying, or a move action by the bloodlord to end the ability. Ending the ability is purely a mental action.

The amount of hit points lost due to blood burn, including when first activated, increases by 1 at 3rd level and again every 4 levels thereafter, to a maximum of 6 at 19th level. This value cannot be altered or reduced by any other effects unless it is explicitly stated that it alters the numerical value of blood burn or by the bloodlord as described below.

At the beginning of their turn, a bloodlord may choose to take a lower value of blood burn until the beginning of their next turn. This lower value cannot be lower than 1, however.

The effects of the augmentations for several of the bloodlord’s class abilities are dependent on the numerical value of the bloodlord’s current blood burn suffered each turn. The augmentations only apply if their blood burn is active. The bloodlord can only have one augmentation in effect each round, chosen at the time they take damage from their blood burn. The damage caused by blood burn does not trigger any concentration checks.

Augmentation: Any other source that causes a loss of hit points, such as taking damage from an attack, ability, or effect, has that loss of hit points inflicted upon the bloodlord reduced by the value of the blood burn, to a minimum of 1 hit point loss. This adjustment to the loss of hit points caused by a source other than the bloodlord’s own blood burn is applied for each instance of hit points lost.

Energy-based damage types, such as acid, cold, electricity, fire, and sonic, nonlethal damage, or damage caused by an effect that does not physically damage the bloodlord are not affected by this augmentation.

Blood Talents

Starting at 1st level and every odd bloodlord class level thereafter, the bloodlord gains a blood talent. The choices available for a blood talent are listed on page 15. Any prerequisites of the blood talent are listed in the description.

Note that a bloodlord’s specialization, as described in sanguine paths, grants them a specific bonus blood talent at 1st level and it allows them to select blood talents from a specific sanguine path at an earlier level.

Some of the blood talents are entirely exclusive to a sanguine path and cannot be chosen without specialization in that sanguine path.

Bloodline Limits: Starting at 2nd level and every even bloodlord level thereafter, the bloodlord gains a bloodline limit. The choices available for a bloodline limit depend entirely on the sanguine path they have chosen to specialize in as described under sanguine paths.

The bloodlord can select Novice Cruomancer feat or one of the feats from Liber Vampyr that has the tag of vampire. Note that the blood points gained via the Novice Cruomancer feat or required for the feats with the vampire tag are not directly interchangeable with the sanguine points blood gained via sanguine recycler.

However, the bloodlord can use 4 sanguine points to gain 1 temporary blood point to immediately use for any of the chosen feats with the vampire tag gained in this way.

For prerequisite purposes, treat the bloodlord’s effective class level as half their bloodlord levels. The bloodlord must meet any other prerequisites of the ability chosen.

The bloodlord uses their Constitution modifier in place of any other ability score modifier for determining the save DC of any ability gained via a bloodline limit.

For example, if a 10th level bloodlord with the heaven of blood thaumaturgy as their selected sanguine path specialization chooses a bonus arcane discovery or bonus metamagic feat for their bloodline limit gained at that level, the bloodlord can select an option available to a 5th level wizard.

Hematologic Recovery

Due to the bloodlord’s familiarity with their own physiology and preliminary experiments with their sanguine recycler and blood bank, they have begun to unlock the secrets behind accelerated natural healing through the consumption of the lingering life force in their blood bank. This form of healing works even if the bloodlord is undead or incorporeal.

Starting at 1st level, as a standard action, a bloodlord can use sanguine points to recover 1 hit point per sanguine point used, to a maximum number of sanguine points used equal to their class level + their Constitution modifier. The bloodlord can use this ability once per day at 1st level, and every 5 class levels thereafter, to a maximum of 4/day at 16th level.

At 5th level and every 4 bloodlord class levels thereafter, the recovered amount of hit points per sanguine point used increases by 1.

Any excess hit points recovered by this ability are lost.

Augmentation (Su)

If the bloodlord activates hematologic recovery while they have their blood burn active, the total amount of hit points recovered increases by an additional amount equal to 10% x the value of their blood burn (rounded down, minimum equal to bloodlord’s Constitution modifier).

For example, if the use of hematologic recovery would normally heal the bloodlord 50 hit points and the value of blood burn is 3, then the additional amount of hit points recovered would be 50 x 30% = 15. The total amount of hit points recovered through hematologic recovery would then be 50 + 15 = 65 hit points.

Sanguine Paths: At 1st level, a bloodlord chooses one of the three available sanguine paths, Legerdemain, Thaumaturgy, or War, as their specialization. This determines the bloodlord’s weapon and armor proficiencies, BAB, additional class skills, a specific bonus starting blood talent, and the list of bloodline limits available to the bloodlord.

In addition, the bloodlord can select a blood talent belonging to the same sanguine path as their specialization at an earlier level, lowering the bloodlord level prerequisite, if any, by 4. Some of the blood talents from the sanguine paths have augmentations that are only possible during a blood burn and some of the blood talents are exclusive to those who selected the relevant sanguine path as their specialization.

Sanguine Recycler (Ex)

Starting at 1st level, the bloodlord gains the ability to draw the blood of others into themselves, capturing the lingering life essence and genetic material residing in their blood. The bloodlord must make a melee touch attack as a standard action that provokes an attack of opportunity. The drawn foreign blood is then compressed and stored in the bloodlord’s blood bank.

The target must be a recent corpse (within 1 minute of death), a living creature that has blood, i.e. not oozes, or an undead or construct filled with or composed of blood, like vampires and blood golems. Additionally, the target must have hit dice equal to or greater than 1/2 the bloodlord’s class level (minimum 1), have a minimum CR of 1/2, and be no greater than 1 size category different than the bloodlord.

This ability has a Fortitude save (DC 10 + 1/2 the bloodlord class levels + their Constitution modifier). The target must always oppose this ability. A successful save negates the withdrawal of blood for the current round.

Creatures and objects normally immune to Fortitude saves are still subject to this ability assuming they are a valid target.

Every consecutive round after the first, the bloodlord may expend a move action to attempt to draw blood from the target again. Maintaining this ability does not provoke an attack of opportunity.

Animal companions, cohorts, followers, familiars, mounts, and allies, even if willing or helpful, still resent being used as “blood bags” – the GM/GM can reasonably rule that mistreating such entities on multiple occasions may be a violation of any bond or contract between them and the individual (whether it be the bloodlord or another character) with whom they share that bond or contract, with the specific consequences being up to the GM/GM.

Examples of such appropriate consequences could be the nullification of the bond, future animal companion options may be no longer available for the individual with the bond or contract (regardless of which class or source granted the class feature), attitudes of individuals becoming one step worse toward the bloodlord, and so forth.

If the bloodlord does not maintain the ability or loses contact because the target has moved away, the ability ends.

When affected by sanguine recycler, the target takes damage equal to 1d6 + the bloodlord’s Constitution modifier. For each d6 of dice of damage dealt, the bloodlord stores 1 sanguine point into their blood bank. If using sanguine recycler on a corpse, no damage is dealt but the bloodlord adds 1 sanguine point per d6 to their blood bank. Once sanguine points have been taken from a corpse, it cannot be targeted by this ability again. Summoned creatures do not provide the bloodlord with any sanguine points when they take damage from this ability.

This ability’s damage dice increases by an additional 1d6 at 5th, 10th, 15th, and 20th level.

Each time a target takes damage from sanguine recycler, they are fatigued for a number of rounds equal to the bloodlord’s Constitution modifier.

This does not increase a fatigue effect to exhaustion, instead the duration of this fatigue condition is renewed.

If a target is fully drained of blood as a result of sanguine recycler, treat the death as caused by a death effect.

Augmentation (Su)

While the bloodlord has their blood burn active, the total amount of sanguine points gained from a target each round by sanguine recycler increases by an amount equal to the value of their blood burn. This addition is calculated last and is not affected by any other multiplier, regardless of source.

Sanguis Aerarium (Ex)

After extensive meditation and self-training, each bloodlord can develop their own sanguis aerarium, a mental construct similar to a memory of loci. The difference is that what it allows the bloodlord to recall is far more bloody.

Starting at 3rd level, whenever the bloodlord successfully obtains sanguine points from killing a living target creature or using it on a target corpse, the genetic information within the target’s blood, including bloodline, natural talents, and memories of learning knowledge, is saved in the bloodlord’s sanguis aerarium in the form of runic scriptures composed of blood that spells out the name of the target if known or another name of the bloodlord’s choosing. These runic scriptures serve as an unique form of memory recall in the sanguis aerarium and are known as a bloodline memory extract (BME).

The uses of a BME saved in the sanguis aerarium are as follows below, with each use requiring spending a number of sanguine points and time for each process:

The bloodlord may spend 1 sanguine point at any time after collecting a BME to make a normal Knowledge check with a +5 bonus to identify the creature type and if they beat the DC by +10, they also identify its blood type. This allows you to get an untrained result above a 10 on your Knowledge check, if applicable. In addition, instead of learning only one piece of useful information for beating the Knowledge DC for every 5 points when identifying the creature’s abilities and weaknesses, you gain instead two pieces of useful information.
When gaining a feat, bloodline limit, skill, or class level, the bloodlord may be able to ignore a training, group membership, or ancestry requirement as long as they have collected a BME from a creature possessing the feat, ability, skill, or class. Doing so requires the expenditure of 10 sanguine points.
Whenever the bloodlord uses an ability or effect, including blood transmogrification, to disguise themselves, they can consult a BME beforehand to perfect their disguise if they wish to appear as the target did when alive. The bloodlord does not gain any specific memories, languages, or intelligence from the BME, but the recall is enough to double the bonus to their Disguise check granted by the ability or effect used to disguise themselves. This applies only to any one such ability or effect at any given time. The bloodlord must spend a number of sanguine points equal to the effective level of the ability or effect and one minute concentrating on consulting the BME in a mental simulation within their sanguis aerarium either immediately before or after using the ability or effect to disguise themselves.
If a BME is from a target that could cast arcane spells while alive, the bloodlord can spend 10 sanguine points per arcane spell level that the target was capable of casting. This process requires 10 minutes per arcane spell level to complete. Thereafter, the bloodlord can choose to learn any of the spells known by the target at the time of death, if spontaneous caster, or had prepared on the day of their death, if prepared caster, as described under minor sanguis magicae if the spell belongs to the bloodlord spell list.
The bloodlord can utilize a BME for their ultimate bloodlord class ability, sanguis sanguinem parit.
Sanguis Sanguinem Parit (Ex)

At 20th level, the bloodlord achieves the pinnacle of modifying and refining their own bloodline and genes, bringing rise to their mantra, “Blood begets blood.” So long as the bloodlord has a BME saved in their sanguis aerarium, the bloodlord can gain almost all of the racial traits of the original creature from which the BME was extracted via sanguine recycler, including the physical features and subtypes. They do not gain the racial ability score modifiers, spell-like abilities, supernatural abilities, and creature type from the BME. The bloodlord can only gain these benefits from one BME at any given time while this ability is in effect.

The race need not be of the same race as the bloodlord, but they must be of the same creature type as the bloodlord’s base creature type or their new creature type if their base creature type was changed by an inherited template.

For example, if the bloodlord’s base creature type as a humanoid was changed to outsider due to a spell granting them the half-celestial template, thus making it an acquired template, for the purposes of this ability, the bloodlord’s creature type is humanoid. If the same bloodlord was a humanoid born with the half-celestial template, thus making it an inherited template, then for the purposes of this ability, their creature type is outsider. Bloodlords who are natural shapechangers, or possess the shapechanger subtype via an inherited template, and can change their creature type, not merely assume the form of a creature type, treats whatever creature type they possessed at the time of the selection process (see below) as their base creature type for the purposes of this ability.

The bloodlord makes this choice once each day, with the process requiring spending 60 sanguine points and 10 minutes to complete, with the effects of this ability lasting for 24 hours. The bloodlord can select a different saved BME in their sanguis aerarium each day they make this choice if desired. For all relevant purposes and effects, the bloodlord counts as either their race or the race of the BME, whichever is more beneficial for the bloodlord for any given circumstance.

If any of the racial traits from the selected BME is a physical trait, such as extra arms or gills to breathe water, the bloodlord must choose to manifest those physical features in order to gain the benefits of that physical trait. Doing so requires a full-round action to manifest any such physical trait if it was not manifested during the selection process above, and lasts until dismissed as a move action. If dismissed, the bloodlord can choose to manifest that physical trait again as often as desired while this ability is in effect.

This ability is not a transmutation effect nor a polymorph effect, nor does this ability create any magic aura that can be detected. The bloodlord is effectively altering their DNA to express specific traits encoded within a saved BME in their sanguis aerarium. Even spells like true seeing and similar effects will not reveal the two races of the bloodlord when they have this ability in effect. Spells that detect or triggered by specific creature type and subtype will function normally on the bloodlord, if applicable.

Given the wide range of possibilities for this ability, the GM is well within their rights to restrict what races are allowed with this ability in order to maintain campaign stability or game balance.

Favored Class Bonuses

Bloodlords are masters of adapting and enhancing their specialties on their path to bloodline supremacy. As a result, they can select from the following alternative favored class bonuses, regardless of their origin or race:

+1/4 minimum result on sanguine recycler’s damage dice. After taking this favored class bonus 4 times, the bloodlord treats all results of 1s as 2s; after taking it 8 times, treat all results of 1s and 2s as 3s, and so on.
+1/5 of an additional damage die with their sanguine recycler, this increases the number of sanguine points obtained with each successful use of their sanguine recycler as normal.
+1/6 of a new bloodline limit.
+1/6 to the DC of bloodline limits, if any.
+1/6 of a new blood talent.
+1/6 to the DC of blood talents, if any.
+1/3 additional increase to the maximum sanguine points per bloodlord level that their blood bank can hold. This can allow the bloodlord to exceed the normal maximum allowed based on their class level.
+1/6 additional increase to the maximum numeric value granted by the bloodlord’s blood burn. This can allow the bloodlord to exceed the normal maximum allowed based on their class level.
+1/4 to the number of daily uses of hematologic recovery and to the number of hit points recovered per sanguine point spent with hematologic recovery. This can allow the bloodlord to exceed the normal maximum allowed based on their class level.
Any one favored class bonus that is allowed for another class, regardless of origin or race, that the bloodlord already has levels in – the favored class bonus selected applies as normal for that class as if the bloodlord gained a level in that class. This does not allow the bloodlord to exceed any limits, maximums, or restrictions for that class based on levels.
